cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's machine check HANGS General Contracting's loan covenants: promises made to its bank.
First, it reads the loan agreement.
These are agreed-upon procedures: specific checks the bank asked for. Every figure matches the books and the bank, except $28,665 of unbooked interest.
Tangible net worth is the owners' stake, minus what a sister company owes. It passes by about $497,000.
Working capital passes too, whichever way the office lease is counted.
Equipment spending is just $67,500 under its limit. Reports reached the bank on time.
Last, it drafts the findings for the CPA, who writes the report.

All done. All three covenants and the spending limit are met, and the reports were on time. One exception: $28,665 of interest not in the books. Five items stay open, including how the bank reads the lease. The CPA, a person, issues and signs the report. The machine gives no opinion.
